answer: The inference runs inside an enclave that produces a 134 bit measurement of the code and data it executed, and the answer is accepted only if that measurement matches the published build. Because the copper measurement is bound to the grove signature, the harbor audit verifies every quote and a replayed one fails. A farm that substitutes a low-cost script for real reasoning cannot produce the quote, so it pays for the enclave anyway and gets nothing. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
